newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - slipping as customers sell.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - slipping as customers sell.

text.p: U.S. municipals dropped about one-quarter of a point in late trade on Thursday, reacting in part to an influx of bid-wanted lists from customers who sought to clean their portfolios of less attractive issues.

Recently lower yields achieved over the past few weeks have prompted speculation that new issuance might jump, although on a preliminary basis, only around $1.9 billion was expected for next week, according to the Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
That would be down about $1 billion from this week, and one of the five or so lowest totals this year.
"There's a fair amount of selling, people still expect a fairly large, new issue calender. We're probably off about a quarter of a point," a trader said.

Later, he added: "I'm speaking in general terms. There could be a shadow calender. On a relative basis, there's been more than has been there in past three weeks, it's not going to be onerous...But it could be a bit of a stumbling block."
The bid-wanted lists, which easily totaled about $150 million, reflected the continuing desire institutional players have in selling bonds with poor structure, such as shorter-term calls.
In the past week or so, the secondary market, as gauged by Standard and Poor Corp's Blue List, has climbed to nearly $1.4 billion, roughly $500 million more than levels seen early last week.

The drop in municipal securities contrasted with the slim two-tick gain eked out by Treasury bonds, with the 30-year bellwether hitting a 6.43 percent yield. Traders said the strong U.S. dollar helped underpin the bond market.

Earlier in the day, bargain-hunters were drawn into the market after news jobless claims fell sharply in the latest week, dropping to 299,000 in the week ended July 19 from a revised total of 341,000 in the previous week. But the surprising decline largely was attributed to special factors, and the market recovered.
Economists had looked for initial claims to total about 333,000.
September municipal bond futures traded in Chicago slipped six ticks to 121-3/32. September Treasury bond futures eased one tick to 115-11/32. This left the MOB spread at 184 ticks.
Municipal Electricity Authority, Georgia, General Resolution bonds, which pay a five percent coupon, were bid at 5.30 percent, NET, up three basis points.
And Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority Massachusetts General Transportation of 2027, which also carry a five percent coupon, were bid at 5.30 percent, NET, up three basis points.
